caption:
The headline says 25,000 years. Here is the range.
Science Advances, 9 Sept 2026. Brumm, Griffith University; Papke, University of Florida.

Two forager skeletons from Sulawesi: a new tooth-wear pattern and traces of arecoline, from betel nut, a mild stimulant. n = 2. The older one is dated 16,000 to 25,000 years; headlines quote the top. It may be the earliest evidence of drug use. Would you have printed the top of the range?

#archaeology #anthropology #science #history
voiceover_script: The headline says humans got high twenty five thousand years ago. Here is what is actually behind it. Two forager skeletons from Sulawesi, in Indonesia. Two. That is the whole sample. Their teeth show a wear pattern nobody had described before, plus chemical traces of arecoline, which comes from betel nut, today the world's fourth most used psychoactive substance, a mild stimulant. Now the date. The older skeleton is dated somewhere between sixteen thousand and twenty five thousand years. The headlines quote the top of that range. Even so, the authors say it may be the earliest evidence of drug use found so far.
